about: Saint Jude's prisons (J1). Facilities, who they take, the groups inside, and the figures the inside week, channels and reviews weigh. Bible Part II 8 fixes the county jail (unsentenced and short terms), the federal detention center (federal defendants awaiting trial; name Open), Ironhaven (state felons, long terms) and federal penitentiaries elsewhere (Atlanta, Leavenworth, Lewisburg, Danbury, Marion); which mobster does time where is Open. Every figure is a Design proposal and a calibration target, never a cap.

entry_standing.why: Standing inside of a man who held no seat outside (0..1); a man with a seat outside brings his own standing. Unsourced.

county_jail.name: the county jail
county_jail.why: Bible Part II 8: dirty, overcrowded and dangerous; holds the unsentenced and short sentences. Capacity and headcount are Design proposals (headcount above capacity is the bible's overcrowding).

county_jail_women.name: the county jail's women's section
county_jail_women.why: Women are few and held apart (spec 7.2); a separate small section of the jail. Unsourced.

federal_detention_center.name: the federal detention center
federal_detention_center.why: Part II 8 and the Federal Complex: fourteen stories downtown, opened 1974, holds federal defendants awaiting trial; name Open (called the federal detention center in the text). Federal staff are out of the Pad's reach, so corruption is low.

ironhaven.name: Ironhaven
ironhaven.why: Part II 8: the Ironhaven complex upstate holds state felons for long terms.

ironhaven_women.name: Ironhaven's women's unit
ironhaven_women.why: Open in the bible: women state prisoners are few and held apart; authored as a unit at Ironhaven. Unsourced.

lewisburg.name: Lewisburg
lewisburg.why: Opened 1932 [verified]; criticised by a federal judge in 1976 for inmate violence, so rough in 1975. `pull` is the relative weight with which a federal man of that class is sent here rather than to the other penitentiaries (which prison holds which man is Open).

marion.name: Marion
marion.why: Opened 1963 [verified]; a penitentiary in 1975, not yet the end of the line (that dates from 1983), so only the longest federal terms.

danbury.name: Danbury
danbury.why: Opened 1940 [verified]; held both men and women in the 1970s and is lower security (exact class Open); takes the shorter federal terms.

connected.name: the connected men
connected.why: Share of a facility's headcount, normalised over its groups (Design proposal). Men with a seat in an organisation of the life; a made man expects deference (Part II 8).

neighbourhood_north.name: the north side crowd
neighbourhood_north.why: Prison hierarchy follows race and neighbourhood (Part II 8). The engine has no neighbourhood record per man yet, so the two crowds take the rest by a stable per-man draw; a gap named in the J1 report.

street.name: the street crews
street.why: A man with violence on his record and no seat in an organisation.

protective.name: protective custody
protective.why: A man who has informed needs protective custody (spec 7.2).

week.why: The inside week (J1.3). Each rate is per named man per week and is scaled by the facility's own figures; nothing here is a cap or a quota. All unsourced unless marked.

violence_gain.why: Violence rises with crowding: violence = base * (1 + gain * (crowding - 1)), crowding = headcount / capacity (the bible: the county jail is overcrowded and dangerous).

corruption_gain.why: A crowded place is harder to watch: corruption = base * (1 + gain * (crowding - 1)).

rate.why: Weekly chance a named man is in a fight or an infraction, at violence 1.0 and no crowding; the facility's violence scales it.

tension_scale.why: A counterparty from an outfit his own is at odds with weighs 1 + heat * this (org_tension heat, 0..1), so rival crews meet each other far more often than strangers.

same_group_weight.why: A man fights inside his own group less often than outside it.

unnamed_share.why: Chance the other man is one of the unnamed headcount: no case, only the conduct record.

serious_share.why: Share of fights that are serious enough to be recorded as harm (and so go to the law like any crime); the rest are infractions on his record.

severity.why: Harm severity of a serious fight, drawn uniformly.

methods.why: Weights of the method of a serious fight (the lethality data weighs each).

offender_share.why: Chance the man whose week it is, rather than the other, is the one who started it.

rate.why: Weekly chance a facility has a contraband event at contraband 1.0; scaled by the facility figure and by its corruption.

caught_share.why: Share of events in which a named man is caught and it goes on his record; the rest pass.

dues_weekly.why: Dollars a week a man pays his group's shot caller for protection and standing, 1975 prices (a pack of cigarettes a day was the real currency).

commissary_weekly.why: Dollars a week he spends at the commissary if he has the money.

paid_gain.why: A man who pays moves his inside standing this share of the way to 1.

unpaid_loss.why: A man who cannot pay loses this share of his inside standing.

rate.why: Weekly chance a named man gets out, at security factor 1.0: rare.

security.why: How much easier or harder a security class makes it.

corruption_gain.why: A bought guard helps: the chance is multiplied by 1 + gain * corruption.

found_rate.why: Weekly chance that a man who is an active informer is found out by the men inside.

standing_loss.why: A man found to have informed loses this share of his standing in the group he leaves for protective custody (spec 7.2: talking loses it).

channels.why: Channels between a man inside and the outside (J1.4). Visits and letters happen by a weighed pull, never on a schedule. All figures are unsourced design proposals and calibration targets, never caps.

spouse.why: Pull of a spouse's tie to visit.

friend_pull.why: Pull of a friend who feels for him: this times the larger of their affection and trust of him (0..1).

friends_considered.why: How many of the people who feel most for him are weighed each week (bounds the work; the rest do not come).

rate.why: Weekly chance at pull 1.0 and no distance that a person visits: 1 - exp(-rate * pull * distance).

far_factor.why: A facility off the map is far: this multiplies the pull (rarer visits).

cost.why: Dollars a visit costs the visitor (fare and a lost day's work), 1975 prices.

far_cost.why: Extra share of the cost when the facility is far (cost * (1 + this)).

rate.why: Weekly chance at pull 1.0 that he writes or is written to, when no visit happened.

familiarity.why: Per contact, times the channel quality: familiarity of the two.

orders_share.why: Share of a seat-holder's contacts that carry orders to his outfit.

intercept_rate.why: Chance orders are overheard at watched 1.0: this times the channel's watched share.

use_rate.why: Weekly chance a standing channel (trusted man, phone, note, guard, lawyer) is used.

quality.why: A visit carries a message fairly well.
A lawyer carries a message and the law's own news.
A man of his outfit who visits as a friend.

open_rate.why: Weekly chance one of his outfit's men takes up the route.

quality.why: A guard who carries what he is given.

watched_weight.why: How much of a channel's worth a watch takes away: quality * (1 - weight * watched).

recency_days.why: Half-life of a channel's worth by days since it was last used.

outside.why: What the outside does while a man is inside (J1.5). Unsourced design proposals, never caps.

decay_weekly.why: Share of his standing outside he loses each week with no channel at all; a good channel (grip) holds it: loss = decay * (1 - grip).

envelope_weekly.why: Dollars a week the head of his outfit pays his household at standing 1.0 and the first week held, 1975 prices (the outfit looks after its own).

envelope_halflife_weeks.why: The envelope halves each this many weeks he is held: the longer, the thinner.

envelope_floor.why: Below this many dollars the outfit stops paying.

need_weekly.why: Dollars a week his household needs, 1975 prices.

cover_weeks.why: Weeks of need that savings must cover for the family not to be going without: need = exp(-savings / (cover * weekly need)).
